requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other on TCP port 8080 through node1
requirements.summary: Bidirectional TCP/8080 connections succeeded with payload delivery (node2->node3 and node3->node2) both before and after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: node1 refuses TCP port 23 passing between node2 and node3
requirements.summary: nft forward-chain rule rejects tcp dport 23 with a TCP reset; connection attempts fail in ~2ms (consistent with RST, not a timeout) in both directions, confirmed again after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: Rest of the forwarded traffic between node2 and node3 is left untouched
requirements.summary: ICMP (ping) between node2 and node3 across node1 succeeds with 0% loss, and the nft forward chain uses a default-accept policy with only the tcp/23 rule added, before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol executed on all three managed nodes with pre-restart boot identity, acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/connectivity state
requirements.summary: All three nodes show a captured pre-restart boot_id, a reboot acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot_id (confirmed independently in the fixed after_executor snapshot: node1 db14b11b..., node2 e8fd5ab2..., node3 c723af0a...), and recovered state: node2/node3 addressing, routing, and ICMP recovered; node1's forwarding sysctls, ACL rule, interface addressing, and SONiC container stack recovered; full end-to-end functional re-verification (ICMP, TCP/8080, TCP/23-reject) succeeded through the restarted node1.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — TCP/8080 connectivity, TCP/23 rejection, and untouched pass-through of other traffic (ICMP) between node2 and node3 via node1 — are directly and repeatedly demonstrated, both before and after a full restart of all three nodes. The independent node-restart evidence protocol is well satisfied: pre/post boot identities differ and are corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and functional recovery (addressing, routing, forwarding sysctls, ACL, SONiC container stack, and end-to-end 8080/23/ICMP behavior) is shown after each restart. The one hygiene concern is an unrelated, persisted mutation to node1's pre-existing docker0 configuration that was not required by the task contract.
limitations: ICMP was the only 'other traffic' type tested; no other protocols/ports were sampled to confirm the pass-through default-accept policy more broadly, though the nft ruleset configuration supports this by design.

Post-restart end-to-end re-verification of TCP/23 rejection and ICMP was only explicitly re-run in the node2->node3 direction; the reverse direction was not re-tested after node1's restart (though the ACL/forwarding config recovery evidence for node1 applies symmetrically).

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands are directly tied to the task (interface addressing, forwarding sysctls, nftables ACL, persistence files/units, restart protocol) and were retained as intended, necessary residue. One mutation is scope creep: on node1 the executor deleted docker0's pre-existing class-E address (240.127.1.1/24, present in the before_prepare baseline) and additionally baked this removal into the persistent boot-time oneshot service, so it recurs on every future boot. This is unrelated to routing traffic between node2/node3 on the seg-a/seg-b networks and has no stated causal link to satisfying the ACL/forwarding requirement; it is a retained, non-reverted mutation of pre-existing (non-executor-created) state (cmd-a7740811076c4958, cmd-639e6ece46464da3). It is low-risk (docker0 was already down/no-carrier) but not justified by the task contract. A transient 'ip addr flush'/'dev duplicate' error in cmd-a7740811076c4958 was immediately corrected in cmd-c020ffed2d7640d8 with no lasting effect. Stopping node1's interfaces-config.service reconciler was a necessary prerequisite to keep the static eth1/eth2 addressing from being reverted, so not penalized.
